findings.claim: The observed landmark_00_soft_mass curve over the full support 0.0-0.49 is non-monotone: it rises from about -0.37 z early, peaks near +1.64 z around t~0.16, then declines to about -0.28 z at the end, with 4 sign changes and no accepted polynomial.

Across the full observed score window (0.0-0.49), no landmark soft_mass feature shows a stable whole-window displacement: every whole_window_z is small in magnitude (|z| < 0.65) and no polynomial is accepted, so the endpoint coordinate features are not stationary targets but fluctuating contrasts.

Several landmarks show large-magnitude early-window rates that reverse sign by the late window (e.g. landmark_00 first_rate_z ~ +9.3 vs last_rate_z ~ -10.0; landmark_03 ~ -61.0 vs +12.7; landmark_11 ~ -66.3 vs +10.8; landmark_10 ~ +66.3 vs -11.6), indicating non-monotone temporal contrasts rather than a single sustained drift.

Sign-change counts are high (4-10) and strong_sign_conflicts are nonzero for nearly all landmarks, so the observed temporal contrasts are not consistent across independent batches; the 14 independent batches do not support a single signed direction.

The learning window and observed score times span 0.0-0.5 with 50 observed score nodes, and the label semantics are recorded affinities removed with an equal score prior; the coordinate features are predicted endpoint world coordinates, not decoded affinities.

hypotheses.direction: no single signed direction supported; treat as fluctuating contrast
hypotheses.falsifier: A recipe that produces a stable whole-window z with |z| substantially larger than the observed |z| < 0.65 and no sign reversal would contradict this.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass predicted endpoint world coordinate feature
hypotheses.scope: landmark_00 across the full observed window 0.0-0.49
hypotheses.statement: If a temporal reward recipe is applied, it should be evaluated against the observed non-monotone landmark_00_soft_mass contrast rather than assuming a monotone approach to a static coordinate target, because the observed curve rises then falls within the window with 4 sign changes and no accepted polynomial.

hypotheses.falsifier: A recipe that leaves strong_sign_conflicts and sign_changes unchanged while shifting the pooled mean would falsify the claim that batch-consistency is the relevant criterion.
hypotheses.statement: Because strong_sign_conflicts and sign_changes are nonzero for nearly all landmarks, any reward edit should be checked for batch-consistency; a recipe that improves only the pooled mean without reducing cross-batch sign disagreement is not supported by the observed evidence.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are not available; only continuous curve trend rows and one observed curve were read, so no stage-boundary or profile-based conclusion is supported.
No decoded final affinity labels are present (recorded affinities removed; equal score prior), so selection preference cannot be equated with descendant survival or measured final benefit.

The continuous_trends rows and the landmark_00_soft_mass curve report predicted endpoint world coordinate features; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is attached to these untyped coordinate proxies.
Polynomial fits were not accepted for any landmark, so no extrapolation beyond the observed 0.0-0.49 window is supported.
